To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

breastfeeding is the most natural and healthiest way to nourish infants and that the decision to breastfeed and to continue breastfeeding for at least 6months post-partum is influenced by an array personal, social and physiological factors.
breastfeeding is a complex process that is influenced by a variety of factors.

breastfeeding is an important component of maternal care in most mammals and that the initiation of breastfeeding, duration and composition of milk are influenced by ecological constraints as well as maternal and infant physiology and behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how mothers and their infants are able to successfully breastfeed and how this process can be improved.
the physiological, psychological and social processes involved in the transfer of milk between mothers and their young.
the mechanisms that influence the initiation and continuation of breastfeeding and its impact on the health of both mother and infant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
breastfeeding is a complex and dynamic interaction between the mother and the infant, and the mother and the environment.
the benefits of breastfeeding are well documented and that breastfeeding is the optimal form of nutrition for the infant.

the physiological mechanisms, behavioral and psychosocial factors influencing breastfeeding are complex and multifactorial and require further study to fully understand the mechanisms underlying this important form of maternal care.

the decision to breastfeed is influenced by a complex array of personal and social factors that are often difficult to modify, however, breastfeeding is associated with positive outcomes for both mother and infant.
the initiation of breastfeeding is facilitated by the provision of support from health care professionals and family members and the development of a positive attitude towards breastfeeding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is considerable variability in the duration of breastfeeding and in milk production across mammalian species and women.
there is a great deal that is known about the factors influencing the transfer and utilization of breast milk, but much more needs to be learned to facilitate the achievement of breastfeeding goals.
breastfeeding has a profound effect on the health, development and survival of both the infant and mother.
